Letter of May 8, 1972, from Chief, Planning Section, Arizona Department of Economic Planning and Development.
Comment: This letter incorporates comments received by the State Clearinghouse from various State agencies. In reference to the criteria in the proposed legislation used to define various levels of endangerment, objected to the terms "significant portion of its range" and "likely to become threatened with extinction within the foreseeable future" as too loose.
Response: Comment was requested and is responded to here only on the Environmental Impact Statement and not on the proposed legislation. Definition of the term, "endangered" is a subject of the legislation and not of the EIS. However, this explanation of the term is offered. It is recognized that criteria provided in the proposed legislation do not spell precisely which species fall under terms of the definitions. Purpose of the action is not only to protect and restore only those species that now are critically threatened with extinction but to head off the ultimate plight of species that will soon reach the same point even though they are not rare now. It must be recognized that criteria for endangerment must include more than population levels. A given population may be threatened depending upon (1) what the species is or which taxonomic level is involved; (2) how many separate populations may be involved; (3) present population trends; and (4) the nature of the threat that is responsible for the condition that exists, among other things. In lieu of more stringent, but impractical, criteria, the proposed legislation, as well as current authority, provide guarantees that proposed listings or changes in listing will be discussed with the States or other Federal agencies involved.
